Mesillat Yesharim 4:1:
The Way of Acquiring Watchfulness
Now, what brings a person to watchfulness is the study of Torah. This is what Rabbi Pinchas said at the beginning of the baraita: Torah leads to watchfulness.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:2: However, in particular, what brings this about is reflection upon the seriousness of the service that a person is obligated in, and the depth of the judgment concerning it. And this comes to him from studying the deeds recorded in the holy books, and from studying the sayings of the Sages, of blessed memory, that arouse one to this.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:3: Now, within this reflection there are gradations of arousal: for those complete in understanding, for those lesser than they, and for the masses as a whole. For those complete in understanding, their arousal will come from what becomes clear to them — that perfection alone is the thing that ought to be desired, and nothing else, and that there is no evil greater than the lack of perfection and distance from it.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:4: For once this becomes clear to them, and it likewise becomes clear to them that the means to it are good deeds and good character traits, it is certain that they will never consent to diminish these means or to be lenient with them. For it has already become clear to them that if these means are lessened for them, or if the means are weak and not with all the strength required in them, then they will not attain true perfection through them, but will fall short in proportion to how they fell short in their effort, and they will find themselves lacking perfection — which is for them a great distress and a great evil.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:5: Therefore they will choose only to increase these means and to be stringent in all their conditions, and they will not rest or be at ease from worry lest something be lacking to them that would bring them to the perfection they desire. This is what King Solomon, peace be upon him, said (Proverbs 28:14): "Happy is the man who fears always," which our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Berachot 60a): this refers to words of Torah.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:6: Now, the culmination of this level is what is called Fear of Sin, which is one of the most praiseworthy of the levels; and it is that a person should be always fearful and worried lest there be found in his hand some trace of sin that would hold him back from the perfection he is obligated to strive for.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:7: And concerning this our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Bava Batra 75a): by way of a parable — this teaches that each one is scorched by the sight of his fellow's wedding canopy. For this is not on account of jealousy, which occurs only among those lacking understanding, as I will write further, with the help of Heaven, but rather because he sees himself lacking a level of perfection which he could have attained, just as his fellow attained it.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:8: Now, in light of this reflection, one who is complete in understanding will surely not refrain from being watchful in his deeds.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:9: But for those lesser than these, their arousal will accord with their own perception, namely, in the matter of the honor that they desire.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:10: For this is obvious to every person of faith, that the levels in the true world, which is the World to Come, are divided only according to deeds; and that none is elevated there except one who has more deeds than his fellow, while one who has few deeds will be the lowly one.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:11: If so, then, how could a person shut his eyes to his own deeds, or lessen his effort in this, when afterward he will certainly be distressed at a time when he can no longer rectify what he has twisted?
Mesillat Yesharim 4:12: Now, there are some among the fools who seek only to make things easier for themselves, who say: Why should we exert ourselves with so much piety and abstinence? Is it not enough for us that we not be among the wicked who are punished in Gehinnom? We will not press ourselves to enter the innermost chambers of the Garden of Eden. If we will not have a great portion, we will have a small one. This is enough for us, and we will not burden our load for this.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:13: However, let us ask them one question: could they so easily bear, in this fleeting world, to see one of their fellows honored and exalted more than they, and ruling over them — and all the more so one of their own servants, or one of the despised and lowly poor in their eyes — without being pained, without their blood boiling within them? No, certainly not!
Mesillat Yesharim 4:14: For our own eyes see it: all of man's labor is to be raised above whoever he can, and to place himself among the higher ones — for it is jealousy of a man toward his fellow. And if he sees his fellow rising while he himself remains lowly, certainly what he suffers is what he is forced to suffer, for he cannot prevent it, and his heart breaks within him.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:15: Now, if it is so hard for them to be lowlier than others in imagined and false rank — where the lowliness itself is only outward, and the elevation nothing but vanity and falsehood — how could they possibly bear to see themselves lower than those very people who are now lower than they, in the place of true rank and eternal preciousness? For even though they do not now recognize it and its worth, and therefore give it no heed, yet in its proper time they will surely recognize it in its truth, to their grief and their shame; and this will certainly be for them nothing but a great and eternal anguish.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:16: Behold, then, that this patience which they seek for themselves, to lighten upon them the weight of the service, is nothing but a false enticement with which their inclination entices them, and not a true matter at all.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:17: And indeed, this enticement would have had no place with them, were they to see the truth of the matter. But since they do not seek it out, and go about erring according to their own desire, their enticement will not be removed from them until the time when it will be of no avail to them, for they will no longer have it in their power to rectify what they have corrupted. This is what King Solomon, peace be upon him, said (Ecclesiastes 9:10): "Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with all your might, for there is no deed, nor reckoning, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave (Sheol) where you are going."
Mesillat Yesharim 4:18: That is, whatever a person does not do while the power is still given to him by his Creator — the power of free choice given to him all the days of his life, in which he is a free agent and commanded to act — he will no longer be able to do it in the grave and in Sheol, for this power will no longer be in his hand; for whoever has not done many good deeds in his lifetime cannot do them afterward. And whoever has not reckoned an accounting of his deeds will have no time to reckon it then. And whoever has not grown wise in this world will not grow wise in the grave. This is what it says: "For there is no deed, nor reckoning, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave (Sheol) where you are going."
Mesillat Yesharim 4:19: But the arousal for the masses as a whole is with regard to reward and punishment themselves, seeing how deep the judgment reaches — which is truly cause to tremble and be in constant dread, for who can stand on the Day of Judgment, and who can be found righteous before his Creator, whose scrutiny is exacting over every matter, small or great?
Mesillat Yesharim 4:20: And so our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Chagigah 5b): "And He declares to man what is his speech" (Amos 4:13) — even a light conversation between a man and his wife is declared to a person at the time of judgment.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:21: They also said (Yevamot 121b): "And it is very tempestuous round about Him" (Psalms 50:3) — this teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, is exacting with His pious ones to a hairsbreadth.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:22: Abraham — that same Abraham beloved of his Maker, of whom Scripture says (Isaiah 41:8), "Abraham My friend" — did not escape judgment for light matters in which he was not exacting with himself. Because he said, "Whereby shall I know?" (Genesis 15:8), the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: By your life, know for certain that your seed shall be a stranger (Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 48). Because he made a covenant with Avimelech without the command of the Omnipresent (Bereishit Rabbah 54), the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: By your life, I will delay the joy of your children for seven generations (ibid. 89).
Mesillat Yesharim 4:23: Jacob — because his anger flared against Rachel when she said to him, "Give me children," they said in the Midrash, in these words: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: Is this how one answers the distressed? By your life, your children will one day stand before her son (ibid. 71).
Mesillat Yesharim 4:24: And because he put Dinah in a chest so that Esau would not take her — even though his intention was certainly for the good — nevertheless, because he withheld kindness from his brother, they said in the Midrash (ibid. 76): The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: "To him that is ready to faint, kindness is due from his friend" (Job 6:14) — you did not seek to marry her to a circumcised man, and behold, she was married to an uncircumcised one; you did not seek to marry her off in a permitted way, and behold, she was taken in a forbidden way.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:25: Joseph — because he said to the chief butler, "But remember me when it shall be well with you" (Genesis 40:14), two more years were added to his imprisonment, as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (ibid. 89). Joseph himself — because he embalmed his father without the permission of the Omnipresent, or because he heard his brothers say "your servant our father" and remained silent — whichever explanation one prefers — died before his brothers (ibid. 100).
Mesillat Yesharim 4:26: David — because he called words of Torah "songs" (zemirot), he was punished, in that he stumbled over the matter of Uzza and his rejoicing was thrown into confusion (Sotah 35a).
Mesillat Yesharim 4:27: Michal — because she rebuked David for dancing in the street before the Ark, she was punished that she had no child except at her death (II Samuel 6).
Mesillat Yesharim 4:28: Hezekiah — because he showed the treasure house to the officers of the king of Babylon, it was decreed concerning his sons that they would be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon (II Kings 20).
Mesillat Yesharim 4:29: And there are many more like these.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:30: And in the chapter "Ha-kol Chayavin" they said (Chagigah 5b): Rabbi Yochanan, whenever he reached this verse, would weep: "And I will draw near to you for judgment, and I will be a swift witness, etc." (Malachi 3:5) — a servant against whom light matters are weighed the same as grave ones — can he have any remedy?
Mesillat Yesharim 4:31: And certainly it is not the intention of this statement that the punishment for both should be the same, for the Holy One, blessed be He, repays only measure for measure. Rather, the matter is that with regard to the weighing of deeds, light ones ascend on the scale just as grave ones do, for the grave ones do not cause the light ones to be forgotten, nor does the Judge shut His eye from them at all, just as He does not shut it from the grave ones;
Mesillat Yesharim 4:32: but He watches over and scrutinizes all of them equally, judging each one of them and afterward punishing for each one according to what it is. This is what King Solomon, peace be upon him, says (Ecclesiastes 12:14): "For God shall bring every deed into judgment, etc." — for just as the Holy One, blessed be He, does not fail to remember every small good deed exactly as it is, so too He will not fail to judge and reprove every small evil deed exactly as it is.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:33: And this is to remove from the heart of those who wish to be enticed and to think that the Master, blessed be He, does not bring light matters into His judgments and does not reckon them. Rather, the rule is (Bava Kamma 50a): whoever says the Holy One, blessed be He, is lenient (vatran) — his own life shall be forfeited. And so they said: if the evil inclination tells you, "Sin, and the Holy One, blessed be He, will forgive you" — do not listen to it.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:34: And this is a simple and clear matter, for the Lord is a God of truth (cf. Jeremiah 10:10). This is what Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, said (Deuteronomy 32:4): "The Rock, His work is perfect, for all His ways are justice; a God of faithfulness and without iniquity, etc." For since the Holy One, blessed be He, desires justice, it would be a perversion of justice to overlook merit just as it would be to overlook liability. Therefore, if He desires justice, He must give to every man according to his ways and according to the fruit of his doings, with the utmost exactness, whether for good or for its opposite — that is, "a God of faithfulness and without iniquity, just and right is He" — which our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Sifrei): to the righteous and to the wicked — for such is the measure, and He judges all and punishes for every sin, and there is no escape.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:35: And should you say: if so, then what place does the attribute of mercy occupy, since in any case one must be exacting in judgment about everything? The answer is: certainly, the attribute of mercy is what sustains the world, for without it the world could not exist at all. And nevertheless, the attribute of justice is not compromised. This is because, by the strict letter of the law,
Mesillat Yesharim 4:36: it would have been proper for the sinner to be punished immediately, right at the moment of his sin, without any delay whatsoever.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:37: And also that the punishment itself should be delivered in fierce wrath, as is fitting for one who defies the word of the Creator, blessed be His Name.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:38: And that there should be no remedy for the sin at all.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:39: For indeed, how could a person rectify what he has twisted, once the sin has already been committed? If a person has murdered his fellow, if he has committed adultery — how can this matter be rectified? Can he remove the deed already done from reality?
Mesillat Yesharim 4:40: However, the attribute of mercy is what grants the opposite of the three things we have mentioned:
